The soldiers demanded that the Company withdraw from Madras.
The mutiny led directly to the annexation of the Carnatic in 1801.
x: When the Nizam was at Rajamahendravaram, his army at Gollapudi mutinied over unpaid pay. Jogipantulu used this situation to negotiate the lease of the Circars.
tq: Connect the immediate cause of the crisis with its political consequence.
sec: Intermediaries in the Circar lease - Kandregula Jogipantulu  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which statement about Kandregula Jogipantulu is correct?
o: He was the Mughal emperor who issued the firman for the Circars.
He was a dubashi who acted as an envoy between the Nizam's court and the Company's representatives.
He was the military officer who suppressed the Rayalaseema poligars.
He was the Nawab of Carnatic appointed by the Company after the Second Carnatic War.
x: Kandregula Jogipantulu was a prominent dubashi and envoy who acted between the Nizam's court and the Company's men at Machilipatnam.
tq: Identify the intermediary by his office and function, not merely by name.
sec: Intermediaries in the Circar lease - Kandregula Jogipantulu  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Guntur Circar was held by which person before its eventual transfer to the Company?
o: Muhammad Ali, the Nawab of Carnatic
x: Guntur, the fifth Circar, was held by Basalat Jung, the brother of Nizam Ali.
tq: Use the holder–territory association and avoid confusing the Nizam's family member with Carnatic rulers.
sec: Guntur Circar - circumstances of transfer  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which combination correctly describes the final transfer of Guntur to the Company?
o: Basalat Jung died in 1782; the transfer followed payment of 7 lakh rupees on 18 September 1788.
Basalat Jung died in 1788; the transfer followed payment of 9 lakh rupees in 1798.
Basalat Jung died in 1766; the transfer followed payment of 15 lakh rupees in 1768.
Basalat Jung died in 1800; the transfer followed the Cession Treaty.
x: Basalat Jung died in 1782. Nizam Ali received 7 lakh rupees and handed Guntur over on 18 September 1788.
tq: Match the two dates and the payment figure as a single transfer sequence.
sec: Guntur Circar - circumstances of transfer  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Nellore and Chittoor were once under which ruler before becoming part of the Carnatic?
x: Nellore and Chittoor were once under Aravidu Sriranga Raya III and later formed part of the Carnatic.
tq: Match the earlier regional ruler with the territory before its Carnatic association.
sec: Carnatic districts (Nellore, Prakasam area, part of Chittoor) - year, ruler  [GROUP-II]

s: After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed whom as the Nawab of the Carnatic?
x: After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed Muhammad Ali as Nawab of the Carnatic, though his position became secure only after 1763.
tq: Distinguish the ruler installed after the war from the later Nawab who signed the treaty.
sec: Carnatic districts (Nellore, Prakasam area, part of Chittoor) - year, ruler  [GROUP-II]

s: Which group of powers did the British protect Muhammad Ali from after installing him as Nawab of the Carnatic?
o: Shah Alam II, Salabat Jung and Basalat Jung
Najibullah of Nellore, the Marathas and Hyder Ali
The French, the Portuguese and the Dutch
The Kurnool Nawabs, the Banganapalle chief and Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy
x: The British shielded Muhammad Ali from Najibullah of Nellore, the Marathas and Hyder Ali.
tq: Select the complete set of political and military opponents mentioned together.
sec: Carnatic districts (Nellore, Prakasam area, part of Chittoor) - year, ruler  [GROUP-II]

s: The Carnatic Treaty was signed with which Nawab?
x: The Carnatic Treaty was signed with Nawab Azim-ud-Daula.
tq: Avoid the ruler-swapping trap between Muhammad Ali and Azim-ud-Daula.
sec: Carnatic districts (Nellore, Prakasam area, part of Chittoor) - year, ruler  [GROUP-II]

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Treaty or grant)
A. Salabat Jung's grant
B. Circar lease through Jogipantulu
C. Treaty of Masulipatnam
D. Treaty of Hyderabad

List-II (Year)
1. 1759
2. 1766
3. 1768
4. 1798

The correct code is:
x: Salabat Jung's grant belongs to 1759, the Circar lease to 1766, the Treaty of Masulipatnam to 1768 and the Treaty of Hyderabad to 1798.
tq: Start from the sure date pair and eliminate codes that reverse the neighbouring treaty years.
sec: Treaties with the Nizam - terms, peshkash, Subsidiary Alliance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Under the Treaty of Masulipatnam of 1768, which arrangement was made?
o: The Nizam handed over Guntur after receiving 7 lakh rupees.
The Company leased the Circars for an annual payment of 15 lakh rupees.
The Nizam ceded all the Ceded Districts in lieu of the subsidiary subsidy.
The Company retained the Circars for a reduced peshkash of 9 lakh rupees annually and provided military help to the Nizam.
x: The Treaty of Masulipatnam allowed the Company to retain the Circars for a reduced annual peshkash of 9 lakh rupees, along with military assistance to the Nizam.
tq: Separate the terms of the 1768 treaty from the earlier lease and later cession.
sec: Treaties with the Nizam - terms, peshkash, Subsidiary Alliance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Under the Treaty of Hyderabad of 1798, what was the principal obligation of the Nizam?
o: To provide the Company with a Mughal firman
To pay 15 lakh rupees annually for the lease of the Circars
To surrender Guntur immediately after Basalat Jung's death
To maintain a British subsidiary force and pay for it
x: The 1798 Treaty of Hyderabad required the Nizam to keep a British subsidiary force and meet its expenses.
tq: Match the treaty with its distinctive obligation instead of its date alone.
sec: Treaties with the Nizam - terms, peshkash, Subsidiary Alliance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The Ceded Districts were given to the Company in 1800 in lieu of:
o: The expenses of the Carnatic War
The annual lease payment of 15 lakh rupees
The subsidy payable for the British subsidiary force
The reduced peshkash of the Northern Circars
x: In 1800, the Ceded Districts were transferred to the Company in lieu of the subsidy payable for the subsidiary force.
tq: Distinguish the compensation arrangement from the separate peshkash and lease payments.
sec: Treaties with the Nizam - terms, peshkash, Subsidiary Alliance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which tax was imposed on inland transit and customs duties on goods?
x: Sayer was the tax imposed on inland transit and customs duties on goods.
tq: Discriminate among the four revenue terms by the taxable activity.
sec: Company taxes - Moturpha, Sayer, Abkari, Peshcush  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Abkari was primarily an excise imposed on:
x: Abkari was the excise levied on liquor and toddy.
tq: Match the tax name with the specific commodity or activity on which it was imposed.
sec: Company taxes - Moturpha, Sayer, Abkari, Peshcush  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Moturpha was levied mainly on which of the following?
o: Trades and occupations such as looms, shops and artisan activities
x: Moturpha was imposed on trades and occupations, including looms, shops and artisans. It was not a salt tax.
tq: Separate the look-alike revenue terms by identifying the actual taxable activity.
sec: Company taxes - Moturpha, Sayer, Abkari, Peshcush  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The 1861 petition of the Madras Native Association complained specifically about which tax?
x: The Madras Native Association's petition of 1861 complained about the burden of Moturpha.
tq: Link the dated petition to the particular tax rather than to a general revenue category.
sec: Company taxes - Moturpha, Sayer, Abkari, Peshcush  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Before the Northern Circars were acquired, the Company had factories and godowns at which stations?
x: The Company maintained factories and godowns at Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam before acquiring the Circars.
tq: Use the paired coastal stations rather than inland administrative centres.
sec: Chiefs and Councils system - Masulipatnam, Vizagapatnam  [GROUP-II]

s: Which body governed the Circars at the stations of Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam before district Collectors replaced it?
x: Provincial Chiefs and Councils at Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam governed the Circars before the district Collector system replaced them.
tq: Identify the administrative body by its station-level composition and function.
sec: Chiefs and Councils system - Masulipatnam, Vizagapatnam  [GROUP-II]

s:
Consider the following statements about the early administration of the Circars:
1. Provincial Chiefs and Councils governed the Circars at the principal Company stations.
2. The body was also referred to as the Board of Revenue.
3. District Collectors replaced this arrangement in 1794.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The station-level Chiefs and Councils were also described as the Board of Revenue, and district Collectors replaced them in 1794.
tq: Verify the institutional name, function and date as separate administrative facts.
sec: Chiefs and Councils system - Masulipatnam, Vizagapatnam  [GROUP-II]

s: The Circuit Committee, while examining revenue administration in the Andhra region, recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of ryotwari by permanent settlement
Abolition of the auction system of revenue collection
Continuation of the auction system with higher minimum bids
Transfer of revenue collection entirely to village panchayats
x: The Circuit Committee recommended against the highest-bidder auction system because it harmed both the government and the ryots. Munro subsequently abolished auctions in Rayalaseema.
tq: Identify the recommendation by linking the committee with the administrative problem it addressed.
sec: Circuit Committee - purpose, findings

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the judicial hierarchy in the Madras Presidency?
x: The Munsiff Court functioned at the taluk level, while the Zilla Court functioned at the district level. Sadar Adalats were apex courts for natives at Madras.
tq: Use the administrative level as the anchor for matching the court.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s: The Zilla or District Court functioned under a District Judge. The post of District Judge was created by the:
x: The post of District Judge was created under the Cornwallis Code of 1793. The Madras Regulations of 1816 related chiefly to Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
tq: Use the legislation–office association and reject neighbouring judicial enactments.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s:
With reference to the judicial system in the Madras Presidency, consider the following statements:
1. The powers of the Provincial Courts of Appeal or Circuit Courts were expanded in 1820.
2. The Sadar Adalat dealt with civil cases and the Sadar Faujdari Adalat dealt with criminal cases.
3. Both Sadar courts functioned at Madras as apex courts for natives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Provincial appellate powers were expanded in 1820, while the Sadar Adalat and Sadar Faujdari Adalat were the civil and criminal apex courts for natives at Madras.
tq: Check each court by its level, jurisdiction and location before selecting the code.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s: The Madras Supreme Court established in 1801 primarily exercised jurisdiction over:
o: All village panchayats in the Ceded Districts
Revenue disputes only in the Northern Circars
Native subjects throughout the Madras Presidency
x: The Madras Supreme Court, established in 1801, dealt with British subjects in Madras town. It was distinct from the Sadar courts for natives.
tq: Distinguish courts by their subject jurisdiction and territorial coverage.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of the Indian High Courts Act, 1861, in the Madras Presidency?
o: It replaced the Sadar courts with the Madras High Court in 1862.
It transferred all civil powers from District Judges to Collectors.
It created the first Munsiff courts in every large village.
It established the Madras Supreme Court and abolished the Sadar courts.
x: Under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861, the Madras High Court was established in 1862 and replaced the Sadar courts.
tq: Separate the year of the Act from the year in which the court came into existence.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. CPC — 1859
2. IPC — 1860
3. CrPC — 1861
x: The Civil Procedure Code was associated with 1859, the Indian Penal Code with 1860 and the Criminal Procedure Code with 1861.
tq: Test the coded year associations individually rather than relying on the sequence alone.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s: The introduction of British judicial procedure in place of village panchayats was criticised mainly because it:
o: was slow and costly and contributed to litigation and debt
made justice quicker and less expensive
reduced litigation and eliminated rural debt
transferred all judicial powers to hereditary village officers
x: British judicial procedure displaced village panchayats and was criticised as slow and costly. It increased litigation and contributed to indebtedness.
tq: Select the option that combines all the stated consequences without reversing the criticism.
sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Thomas Munro:
1. He was the President of the Judicial Commission in 1814.
2. The report of the Judicial Commission was submitted in April 1816.
3. Most of the recommendations in the report were accepted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Munro presided over the Judicial Commission in 1814, whose report was submitted in April 1816 and was largely accepted.
tq: Combine office, date and outcome in a single administrative sequence.
sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

s: The Madras Regulations of 1816 provided for:
o: Abolition of all village-level judicial institutions
Munsiff and Panchayat courts as courts of first instance
Transfer of civil justice from District Judges to Collectors
Creation of the Madras High Court
x: The Madras Regulations of 1816 established Munsiff courts and Panchayat courts in every large village and district as courts of first instance.
tq: Match the regulation with its immediate institutional reform.
sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

s: Under the judicial arrangements associated with Munro's reforms, village officials were permitted to deal with:
x: Village officials handled petty thefts under the reformed arrangements. Serious judicial and appellate matters remained with higher courts.
tq: Distinguish limited local jurisdiction from the powers of higher courts.
sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the separation of judicial and revenue functions in 1816 is correct?
o: Collectors received all criminal and civil powers in the same year.
Munsiffs were abolished and replaced by District Collectors.
Collectors lost their judicial powers, while civil justice remained with District Judges.
District Judges lost civil powers, which were transferred entirely to Collectors.
x: Collectors lost their judicial powers in 1816, and civil justice remained with District Judges. Under the ryotwari arrangement, some magisterial powers later returned to Collectors.
tq: Watch for the reversed authority trap involving Collectors and District Judges.
sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

s: In which year did Magistrates receive powers to punish under the judicial reforms described for the Madras Presidency?
x: Magistrates received powers to punish in 1818. The year 1816 is associated with the separation of Collectors' judicial powers and the establishment of Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
tq: Separate closely connected reform dates before choosing the year.
sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

s: Who created thanas under the supervision of darogas in the early British police administration?
x: Cornwallis created thanas under darogas, who were Indian officers assisted by constables. Darogas were criticised for abusing their power.
tq: Use the founder–institution association and avoid swapping judicial and police reformers.
sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

s:
Consider the following statements about the daroga system:
1. A daroga was an Indian police officer.
2. Darogas were assisted by constables.
3. Darogas were widely known for abusing their power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The daroga system placed Indian officers in charge of thanas with constables assisting them, but abuse of authority was a recognised criticism.
tq: Verify composition, subordinate personnel and criticism separately.
sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

s: In the Madras Presidency, the traditional village watchmen were:
o: placed directly under the Sadar Adalat
abolished and replaced by military courts
supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent
x: Traditional village watchmen continued but were supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent. The force was feared because of corruption.
tq: Distinguish supplementation from abolition or replacement.
sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

s: Munro's police reforms of 1816 transferred police supervision from:
o: Darogas to the Board of Revenue
x: Munro's changes in 1816 transferred police supervision from judges to Collectors. This was part of the reorganisation of administrative powers.
tq: Test the direction of transfer by identifying both the former and new authority.
sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

s: The Madras District Police Act was enacted in:
x: The Madras District Police Act was enacted in 1859. The other years relate to judicial or police-administrative changes mentioned in the same context.
tq: Use the year-specific legislation trap and distinguish it from the judicial enactments.
sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

s: The Madras Board of Revenue was established in:
x: The Madras Board of Revenue was set up in 1786 and became the state-level apex of the revenue hierarchy.
tq: Distinguish the Board's establishment year from the years of territorial acquisition and judicial reform.
sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revenue level)
A. State
B. District
C. Taluk
D. Village

List-II (Officer)
1. Tahsildar
2. Collector
3. Board of Revenue
4. Karanam and Munsab

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The Board of Revenue was at the state level, the Collector at the district level, the Tahsildar at the taluk level and the Karanam and Munsab at the village level.
tq: Start from the sure state and village pairs, then complete the intermediate levels.
sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

s: Which of the following correctly represents the revenue hierarchy between the taluk and village levels?
o: Sub-Collector at taluk level; Board of Revenue at village level
Munsab at taluk level; Tahsildar at village level
Tahsildar at taluk level; Karanam and Munsab at village level
Collector at taluk level; Deputy Tahsildar at village level
x: The Tahsildar was the taluk-level officer, while the hereditary village officers were the Karanam and Munsab.
tq: Compare adjacent administrative levels to detect the reversed hierarchy.
sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the revenue hierarchy?

1. Division — Sub-Collector or Revenue Officer
2. Firka — Deputy Tahsildar or Firka Revenue Inspector
3. District — Collector
x: All three pairs are correct. The hierarchy placed the Collector at the district level, Sub-Collector or Revenue Officer at the divisional level and Deputy Tahsildar or Firka Revenue Inspector at the firka level.
tq: Check each officer against the precise administrative tier.
sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

s: The Andhra Board of Revenue was formed in 1953 primarily to:
o: link the government with the districts after the creation of Andhra State
transfer the Ceded Districts to the Nizam
abolish the office of the District Collector
x: The Andhra Board of Revenue was formed in 1953 after Andhra State was created. It served as a link between the government and the districts.
tq: Identify the institution's purpose from the administrative transition that produced it.
sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

s:
Consider the following statements regarding sericulture in Rayalaseema:
1. British promotion of the crop in the Ceded Districts dates to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
2. Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs.
3. The crop was introduced into Rayalaseema only after the formation of Andhra State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The historical association is with British promotion in the Ceded Districts during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, not only after Andhra State was formed.
tq: Reject the absolute time claim and retain the two historically precise statements.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order in which major territorial components of present-day Andhra took shape under Company rule?

A. Ceded Districts
B. Circars
C. Nellore-Chittoor
D. Guntur
x: The Circars came under Company control in 1766, Guntur in 1788, the Ceded Districts in 1800 and Nellore-Chittoor in 1801.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest territorial changes first, then place the middle events by year.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the territorial contrast under British and Nizam rule?
o: The coast and Rayalaseema passed to the Company, while Telangana remained under the Nizam.
Telangana passed to the Company, while the coast remained with the Nizam.
Rayalaseema remained under the Nizam, while Telangana passed to the Company.
The entire Andhra region remained under the Nizam until 1953.
x: The coast and Rayalaseema came under Company rule, whereas Telangana remained under the Nizam. This produced an important political and administrative contrast within the Telugu-speaking regions.
tq: Use the paired regional contrast and beware of reversing the two territories.
sec: Universal angles

s: The growing divergence between the fertile and educated Circars and the arid and neglected Ceded Districts later influenced debates surrounding the:
x: The contrasting development of the Circars and the Ceded Districts later shaped the Sri Bagh Pact debate. The other pacts belong to different political contexts.
tq: Link a regional socio-economic contrast with the agreement it later influenced.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following statements about Thomas Munro in the Andhra region is correct?
o: He introduced mahalwari settlement from Punjab into the Ceded Districts and died at Hyderabad in 1827.
He introduced permanent settlement from Bengal into the Circars and died at Madras in 1801.
He introduced zamindari in Rayalaseema and died at Nellore in 1816.
He introduced ryotwari from the Bara Mahals into the Ceded Districts and died at Pattikonda as Governor in 1827.
x: Munro brought the ryotwari system from the Bara Mahals to the Ceded Districts. He died at Pattikonda in Kurnool district in 1827 while serving as Governor.
tq: Combine the reformer's policy, source region, destination and death details without swapping settlement systems.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ceded Districts — arid and neglected region
Most Collectors — independent functioning without native subordinates or interpreters
x: Most Collectors depended on interpreters or corrupt native subordinates because they did not know Telugu. Munro and Brown were exceptions; Munro himself was a Telugu-speaking Collector.
tq: Find the option that reverses the general rule and its stated exceptions.
sec: Universal angles

s: The concentration of revenue, magisterial and police powers in the office of the District Collector made the Collector the:
o: pivot of British rule and an agent of the end of village autonomy
hereditary head of the Board of Revenue
chief appellate judge of the Madras Supreme Court
x: By combining revenue, magisterial and police powers, the District Collector became the pivot of British administration. This concentration of authority weakened village autonomy.
tq: Infer institutional importance from the combination of powers held by one office.
sec: Universal angles

s: A plea before the Supreme Court sought a separate revenue judicial service cadre on the ground that revenue officers without legal training should not decide land-title disputes. The plea invoked which constitutional provision?
x: The plea invoked Article 14 and argued that officers without legal training should not adjudicate land-title disputes. The Supreme Court issued notice on the plea.
tq: Identify the constitutional article directly linked to the stated legal argument.
sec: Universal angles

s: Who was identified as the Chief Justice of India when the Supreme Court issued notice on the plea for a separate revenue judicial service cadre?
x: The notice was issued by the Supreme Court under Chief Justice Surya Kant. The plea concerned the adjudication of land-title disputes by revenue officers.
tq: Test the current-affairs office-holder directly rather than confusing it with earlier office-holders.
sec: Universal angles
